A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Cradle2Cane and provide readable text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Relocated material can be matched reliably, including the retained appendices and v2's added Appendix E.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark comparisons, component ablations, qualitative experiments, and a 50-participant user study.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds evaluations on three datasets, threshold sensitivity results, and a background-removal ablation.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same SDXL-Turbo two-pass framework, AdaNI thresholds of 5 and 20, SVR-ArcFace, Rotate-CLIP, and training losses. v2's Algorithm 1 restates the existing procedure; the supplementary variants do not replace the proposed method.

E1.justification: v2 retains the CelebA-HQ and in-the-wild evaluations and adds actual evaluations on AgeDB-30, CACD, and FG-NET in Appendix E.1 and Table 4. This substantially broadens benchmark coverage beyond the original dataset family.

E2.justification: Table 4 newly evaluates StyleCLIP and FaceDNeRF alongside CUSP, SAM, and FADING. The original six-baseline comparison in Table 1 remains unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 adds supplementary protocols using approximately 200 generated images per method per new dataset and matched Carvekit variants trained on 1,000 images for 10 epochs. The original benchmark sampling, metrics, and user-study protocol remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's component ablation and noise-level analysis, v2 adds comparisons of six threshold pairs in Table 5 and a controlled with/without-Carvekit experiment in Table 6. These substantially extend analysis of threshold sensitivity and whether preprocessing explains in-the-wild robustness.

E5.justification: The added tables report point values without introducing repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Existing statistical reporting and the user-study reporting remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 4–6 add substantial new results while Tables 1–2 and the user-study outcomes remain unchanged. Table 4 reports Cradle2Cane age errors of 5.57, 4.63, and 5.79 on AgeDB-30, CACD, and FG-NET; SAM has the lower FG-NET error of 5.33. These are additional evaluations, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: Equations 1–15, the HCS definition in Appendix C.3, and the mathematical assumptions are retained. Algorithm 1 presents existing operations as pseudocode without adding a theorem, proof, or substantive derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about the two-pass design, age–identity balance, efficiency, and in-the-wild generalization. The new experiments support existing claims without redefining the main contribution.

C2.justification: Appendix E.2 newly justifies the retained thresholds by prioritizing age accuracy despite higher identity similarity and HCS under wider thresholds. Appendix E.3 newly attributes robustness primarily to SDXL-Turbo and IDEmb, with Carvekit described as non-essential. Appendix A's limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-code link in the abstract and documents the training budget for the new preprocessing ablation. Existing implementation details in Appendix C are unchanged. The retained checklist still says the full dataset and complete training code cannot be released, leaving the scope of the advertised code availability unclear.

R1.justification: v2 adds eight references, including AgeDB, CACD, StyleCLIP, FaceDNeRF, and additional diffusion/image-editing work. The existing related-work discussion and novelty positioning are otherwise retained.

P1.justification: v2 adds Appendix E, pseudocode, and acknowledgements, updates affiliations and publication information, and moves the checklist before the appendices. The main scientific prose and section sequence remain largely unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 4–6 and an Algorithm 1 display, with localized layout changes and relocation of existing illustrations. The original plots, qualitative examples, and user-study visualization are retained.

improvement.justification: The additional datasets and targeted threshold and preprocessing ablations strengthen empirical support beyond v1's CelebA-HQ-focused evaluation. The gains are limited by sparse settings for the new experiments and an architectural explanation of robustness that the Carvekit control alone cannot establish. The code link improves access information, although the release scope remains unclear.
